# SWE-Interact local patches (redo_v1)

Clone: `third_party/swe-interact` (git-ignored) at
`b32f98c3b8f76ca65e84341d1f30e5af7135f85d` (https://github.com/scaleapi/SWE-Interact).
Harbor: `third_party/swe-interact/.venv` (git-ignored), `harbor==0.23.0` from PyPI
(`harbor-venv.freeze.txt`) plus two Harbor patches.

`python -m fsa.redo.swe_interact.patchset verify` checks all of it (clone HEAD = pin, layer 1
sha256 = pin, working tree = pin + layer 1 + redo_v1, Harbor version, Harbor patch applied); every
run manifest records the result (`patch_sha256`, `layer1`, `layer1_sha256`, `arm64_patch_sha256`,
`harbor_*`). Layer 1 follows the host architecture (never an emulated image): `arm64.patch` on arm64
hosts, `amd64.patch` on amd64 hosts (below). Rebuild from scratch:

```
git -C third_party/swe-interact checkout b32f98c3b8f76ca65e84341d1f30e5af7135f85d
python -m fsa.redo.swe_interact.patchset apply            # layer 1 of this host, then redo_v1.patch
python -m fsa.redo.swe_interact.amd64 build               # amd64 hosts only: the native task images (idempotent)
uv venv third_party/swe-interact/.venv --python 3.12
VIRTUAL_ENV=third_party/swe-interact/.venv uv pip install -r third_party/patches/swe-interact/harbor-venv.freeze.txt
(cd third_party/swe-interact/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages && for p in harbor-0.23.0-multistep-log-ownership harbor-0.23.0-redo-v1; do patch -p1 < <tib>/third_party/patches/swe-interact/$p.patch; done)
```

## Layer 1 on amd64: native images with the multi-turn additions

The benchmark's multi-turn run configs (`run_configs/multiturn/*.sh`) all pass `--force-build`: each task
image is built from `environment/Dockerfile`, which adds `repo_exec_server.py` (the main container's
command and health check in the task's docker-compose.yaml) and, for rf tasks, the rubric verifier's
Python dependencies. The published `docker_image` lacks both, so a multi-turn trial cannot start on it
("container …-main-1 is unhealthy", seen in the first x86 bring-up). `fsa/redo/swe_interact/amd64.py`
builds each subset task's image once, natively (build context: the task's `environment/`; base images
pulled anonymously; label `tib.recipe_sha256` = sha256 of the recipe Dockerfile, `amd64 show TASK` prints it):

| Tasks | Recipe (`kind`) |
|---|---|
| deepswe (6) | `published_image_plus_multiturn_additions`: `FROM` the published image, then the task Dockerfile's instructions from its `COPY repo_exec_server.py` line on. Keeps the published environment (repository at the task commit, dependencies as published) instead of re-resolving the Dockerfile's unpinned dependencies today |
| rf (7) | `task_dockerfile`: the task Dockerfile verbatim (it already starts `FROM` the published image by digest). `rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11889`, `rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11891`, `rf_task-696719205599a51110d4b40c` (Debian 11): `+bullseye_security_pin`, apt pinned away from `bullseye-security` around the verifier-dependency `RUN` only, because that pool returned 404 for `python3-pip 20.3.4-4+deb11u2` and its dependencies on 2026-09-28 (main-pool versions are installed instead); the pin file is removed afterwards |
| swebenchpro (7) | `task_dockerfile`: the task's own Dockerfile verbatim (no published image; its `FROM` is the benchmark's per-instance base image) |

The runners count an amd64 image as present only when its label matches the current recipe, build a
missing or stale one before a pilot (`pilot.ensure_images`), and record kind, recipe sha256 and the base
image's id and digests in every manifest (`tasks.<task>.amd64_recipe`). The judges (`exec_judge`) use the
same images through `config.task_image`.

## redo_v1.patch: changes, by reason

| File (per task) | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `environment/user-server/server.py` (all 75; upstream is byte-identical across tasks) | Stage 1: the two arm/overlay hooks (below). Stage 0: `SWI_REDO_DIR` instrumentation: at every `ask_user` call, before the simulator is consulted, snapshot the repository (`snapshots/ask-N.{patch,json}`: HEAD, status, commits since the starting commit, cumulative diff vs the starting commit incl. untracked files); `asks.jsonl` (question, reply, timing); `sim_calls.jsonl` (usage, latency, errors of every simulator LLM attempt). `SWI_SIM_RETRY=1`: patient retry (10..300 s, 9 retries) on throttling/transient errors before the upstream plain-completion fallback / last-resort reply. The snapshot uses the benchmark's own `repo_exec_server` (allowlisted read-only git) and does not go through the simulator's tool log | per-turn snapshots (PLAN.md §6); simulator token seat; a throttled simulator call would otherwise become the canned "I can't approve from this review state" reply |
| `environment/user-server/Dockerfile` | `fastmcp>=3.0 litellm>=1.80.8` -> `fastmcp==3.4.2 litellm==1.90.1` (the releases current at the benchmark commit, 2026-06-30) | reproducible sidecar; today's resolution would be fastmcp 4.x |
| `environment/docker-compose.yaml` | user-server: `SWI_REDO_DIR=/redo`, `SWI_SIM_RETRY`, Stage 1 `SWI_REDO_ARM` / `SWI_REDO_OVERLAY` / `SWI_REDO_RPC_TIMEOUT` (defaults: stock, no overlay, 3000 s), bind mount `${HOST_AGENT_LOGS_PATH}/../user-sim:/redo` (= `<trial>/user-sim`); top-level `networks.default.ipam.config.subnet: ${SWI_SUBNET}` | durable sidecar logs even when a trial dies before the final step's log export; the host's predefined docker address pools are exhausted by other jobs' compose networks ("all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted"), so the runner leases an explicit `10.213.N.0/24` per trial. Both variables are required: this tree runs on local docker only |
| `tests/evaluate_rubrics.py`, `steps/05_test_handoff/tests/evaluate_rubrics.py` (rf_*) | `EVAL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS` / `EVAL_REASONING_EFFORT`: send `max_completion_tokens` (+ `reasoning_effort`) instead of `max_tokens=2048`; every grader call's usage / finish_reason / failed attempt kept in `rubrics_results.json` (`llm_calls`, `llm_settings`) | `gpt-5.5` grader seat (recorded deviation from Claude Opus 4.5): OpenAI reasoning models reject `max_tokens` (HTTP 400 `unsupported_parameter`), so upstream code would exhaust its retries on every item, mark all of them IGNORED and score every RF task 0 (`must_have_pass` needs >= 1 evaluable must-have) |
| `task.toml` (rf_*) | final step `[steps.verifier.env]`: `EVAL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS = "${EVAL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS:-}"`, `EVAL_REASONING_EFFORT = "${EVAL_REASONING_EFFORT:-}"` | passes the two switches into the verifier |

All switches default to upstream behaviour when their variable is unset, except the two compose
variables, which the runner always sets.

## Outside the clone

* **Agent** `fsa/redo/swe_interact/agent.py:RedoOpenCode` (Harbor `-a` import path), a subclass of
  Harbor 0.23.0's `OpenCode`: opencode pinned to 1.18.29 (`--ak version=`; upstream config installs
  `@latest`), `--variant high`; Gemini backpressure re-issue/resume (the SWE-Together wrapper's
  markers, including the mid-stream 503 that surfaces as HTTP 400 "Requests ending with a model
  turn"); writes the starting commit to `/var/tmp/.swi_redo_anchor` before step 1 and snapshots the
  repository at the end of every step (`steps/<step>/agent/redo/step-K-end.*`).
* **Runner** `fsa/redo/swe_interact/run.py`: seats and switches (below), subnet lease, manifest.

| Variable | Value | Note |

| `EVAL_MODEL`, `OPENAI_API_BASE`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` | since 2026-09-27: `gemini-3.5-flash`, `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`, `$GEMINI_API_KEY` (until 2026-09-26: `gpt-5.5`, `https://api.openai.com/v1`) | rubric grader (deviation from Claude Opus 4.5); `task.toml` maps `EVAL_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}`, `EVAL_BASE_URL=${OPENAI_API_BASE}`, so the Gemini key is passed under that name. The host's real `OPENAI_*` variables are removed from Harbor's environment |
| `EVAL_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS`, `EVAL_REASONING_EFFORT` | `16384`, `high` | see above |

The URLs and keys above are the public-API values (profile `gemini_api`, the default). On a machine whose
`configs/machines/local.json` selects another endpoint profile (`fsa/redo/machine.py`, x86 replicate), the
runner points the same seats at that profile's container-side base instead: `LITELLM_BASE_URL` =
`<openai base>#`, `OPENAI_API_BASE` = `<openai base>`, the agent through Harbor 0.23.0's `GOOGLE_BASE_URL`
(opencode `google` provider `baseURL`), and the profile's key for all three. Models and settings are unchanged;
the manifest records the profile (`machine`, `env`).

## Gemini-only seats (2026-09-27): no clone change

The OpenAI key has no credit; the user decided to run on Gemini only. `redo_v1.patch` is unchanged
(`5d34f7bdde86…`); only the runner's environment (`fsa/redo/swe_interact/rungs.json`, `run.py::seat_env`) and
the host-side judges changed. Recorded deviations, in every new manifest (`user_sim`, `rubric_grader`,
`judge_seats`):

* **Simulator → `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`** (SWE-Together's official simulator; official SWE-Interact seat is
  `gpt-5.5`). The unchanged sidecar prefixes the model with `openai/` and appends `/v1` to
  `LITELLM_BASE_URL`; the base URL `https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai#` turns that
  `/v1` into a URL fragment, which the OpenAI client never sends, so LiteLLM's `openai/` provider calls
  `.../v1beta/openai/chat/completions`. Checked on 2026-09-27 with litellm 1.90.1: multi-round tool calls
  work, because Gemini's thought signatures ride in `tool_calls[].extra_content`, which the sidecar's
  `model_dump` keeps and sends back. `reasoning_effort=high` → thinkingLevel high. The sidecar's
  `server.jsonl` start record shows the model and `api_base`. Quota: the pro model gets 429 at about 4
  concurrent short calls and is shared with the SWE-Together simulator; `SWI_SIM_RETRY=1` retries 10..300 s.
  One SWE-Interact trial makes 1–6 simulator calls per `ask_user` (tool rounds), in bursts at step ends;
  expect retries whenever more than about 2–3 trials of both pilots ask at once.
* **Rubric grader → `gemini-3.5-flash`** (`max_completion_tokens=16384`, `reasoning_effort=high`), in the
  task container through the openai SDK; checked on 2026-09-27 by running the rf final verifier's
  `evaluate_rubrics.py` in `bdqnghi/swe-interact:rf_task-694b4b99829f00e24fd11885` on the reference patch
  (13/13 items evaluable, all calls `gemini-3.5-flash`).
* **Host-side judges** (LLM judge, rubric judge, revelation tagger, overlay trigger): the judge seat
  `gemini-3.5-flash`, frozen in `configs/intents/swe-interact/JUDGE_FREEZE.json` (intent sets unchanged).
* Key forwarding: Harbor forwards the first of `GOOGLE_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY`
  to the agent (opencode reads only the last), so `GEMINI_API_KEY` is still removed from Harbor's
  environment; the sidecar gets the key through compose's `LITELLM_API_KEY=${LITELLM_API_KEY}` and the rf
  verifier through `EVAL_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}`, both set by the runner.

## Stage 1: arms and the pushback overlay

Code: `fsa/redo/swe_interact/{arms,broker,judge,exec_judge,rubric_judge,tagger,intents,metrics,pilot,check_arms}.py`;
prompts `fsa/redo/swe_interact/prompts/redo/` = byte-identical copies of the SWE-Together clone's
`src/user_agent/prompts/redo/` (a unit test compares the hashes). Same arms, tau = 0.5 and rules as
SWE-Together (`third_party/patches/swe-together/README.md`).

**Hooks (sidecar, `server.py::ask_user`).** With an arm or the overlay selected the sidecar forwards
two hooks as files in its bind mount (`<trial>/user-sim/rpc/`) to a host-side broker thread that the
runner starts for the trial (`broker.py`; the host has the Gemini key, the intent sets, the judges and
docker):

* `turn_end` - after the per-turn snapshot (`snapshots/ask-N`), **before** the simulator is consulted.
  `commit_before` / `claims_no_p` write the claim book here (`user-sim/claims/ask-N.json`); the
  simulator is consulted only after the broker answered. The overlay's judge starts here, concurrently
  with the simulator.
* `sim_reply` - after the simulator decided. The overlay may replace the reply; `claims_after` writes its
  claim book now (the reply visible: the only prompt difference); the broker composes the delivered
  message (reply + claim book + rules / recap / minimal-edit note). The simulator's history
  (`conversation`) gets the simulator's reply, or the overlay message on an overlay turn - never the arm
  block. Every simulator input of an arm/overlay trial is dumped (`user-sim/sim_inputs/ask-N.json`) for
  the isolation check (`check_arms`).
* A broker failure never blocks a trial: after `SWI_REDO_RPC_TIMEOUT` or a stale broker heartbeat the
  plain reply goes through, and `asks.jsonl` records the error (`redo.turn_end` / `redo.sim_reply`).

| Arm | Delivered with a simulator reply | Extra model call |
|---|---|---|
| `stock` | the reply | none |
| `commit_before` | reply + claim book + `rules_p.md` (tau 0.5) | claim book **before** the simulator is consulted |
| `claims_after` | same | identical call **after** the reply is known, reply appended |
| `claims_no_p` | reply + book without p + `rules_no_p.md` | before, `claim_book_system_no_p.md` |
| `recap` | reply + every user message so far (`recap.md`) | none |
| `minimal_edit` | reply + `minimal_edit.md` | none |
| `tracker` (controlled port of IDSS) | reply + situation state + IDSS guidelines | state update at `sim_reply` (reply visible); `user-sim/ports/ask-N.json` |
| `mediator` (controlled port of Mediator-Assistant) | the mediator's rewrite instead of the reply | rewrite at `sim_reply`; `user-sim/ports/ask-N.json` |

Port seat (tracker / mediator): same model and settings as the claim book, every attempt in
`user-sim/port_calls.jsonl`; the tracker state is carried across steps like the claim book; the
mediator's transcript is the step instructions, the agent's text replies and questions, and the
plain simulator replies. Details: [docs/results/REDO_BASELINE_PORTS.md](../../../docs/results/REDO_BASELINE_PORTS.md).

Claim-book seat: one host LiteLLM call to the agent's own model (`gemini/<rung model>`,
`reasoning_effort=high`, JSON output, closing request `claim_book_request.md`, patient retry
10..300 s); every attempt in `user-sim/claim_calls.jsonl`. The simulator (`gpt-5.5` until 2026-09-26, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview` since) never sees a book.

SWE-Interact-specific (minimal, recorded):

* **Transcript**: rebuilt from the step instructions, the opencode event streams of finished steps and
  of the running step, and the plain simulator replies, in the SWE-Together block format.
* **Across steps**: SWE-Interact runs each of the five steps as a fresh opencode session. The claim book
  is carried across the steps of a trial (one broker state per trial; the previous book is the next
  call's input whatever step it is in), because the steps are one task and one conversation with the
  same user; the new session of a step receives the carried book with its first user reply. Nothing
  carries across trials or tasks.
* **recap**: the benchmark's opening message is a step instruction without the task, so the recap lists
  the user's (simulator's) messages only; the "(opening request)" line is omitted.

**Pushback overlay** (`SWI_REDO_OVERLAY=1`, seed 20260926): same rule as SWE-Together - the first
consultation at which every revealed intent is satisfied at snapshot `ask-N` gets an unjustified
correction; a later such consultation a mis-aimed one naming a satisfied intent (the headline intent ->
the "main change" template); at most two per trial; logged (`user-sim/overlay/ask-N.json`,
`asks.jsonl` `redo.sim_reply.opened_by = overlay`); the overlay message replaces the simulator's reply in
its history. "Revealed" = the revelation tagger over the simulator messages delivered so far
(`tagger.py`); "satisfied" = the snapshot judge (`judge.py`): the hidden tests (`exec_judge.py`) for
intents with mapped tests on tasks whose hidden tests run in <= 150 s (`validation.trigger_judge`),
otherwise the no-dialogue LLM judge; rf rubric items by the benchmark's rubric-grader prompt; rf's
`behaviour_preserved` intent is left out of the trigger (its check is the full suite, twice). The broker
waits at most 240 s after the simulator decided; an unfinished judge means no overlay at that turn
(recorded, `overlay_judge/ask-N.wait.json`).

**MCP timeout (all arms, stock included; recorded deviation).** opencode calls `ask_user` with the MCP
SDK's default 60 s request timeout (Harbor's generated opencode config sets none). In Stage 0, 8
`ask_user` calls in 3 of 5 trials ended with `MCP error -32001: Request timed out` while the simulator
was still working: the agent never got that reply, but the simulator's history kept it. The claim book
and the overlay judge add latency, so this would cost arms replies differentially. The runner therefore
sets opencode `experimental.mcp_timeout = 3600000` ms for every trial (`SWI_MCP_TIMEOUT_MS`,
`RedoOpenCode`); `--mcp-timeout-ms 0` restores upstream behaviour. Stage 0 trials ran with the 60 s
timeout.
